result:
Both defects accepted and fixed. I verified each myself before editing rather than taking the validator's word.

## [1.1] "fastest cell" mislabel — fixed in the deliverable

Confirmed false from the very source I'd already cited: N5 offers "a high-performance cell at 0.025 µm² and a high-density cell at 0.021 µm²". Calling the HD cell "the fastest" was wrong, and it sat at the hinge of a question whose premise is literally "the fastest materials available".

I took the relabel rather than switching to 0.025 µm², for a substantive reason: the argument needs a **lower bound** on physical size. The densest cell gives the smallest array and so the smallest crossing time — quoting it concedes maximum ground to the premise. Switching to the HP cell would have produced *larger* numbers (2.0e5 mm², 447 mm, 2.98 ns, ~12 cycles — computed, matching the validator's figures) and therefore a weaker piece of reasoning. The new text makes that logic explicit instead of implicit:

> Take the densest cell in production, a 6T SRAM bit at 0.021 µm²; the faster high-performance variant is larger at 0.025 µm², so this keeps the bound conservative.

All seven verified numbers preserved. The same conflation was also in `calc_size_latency.py` (comment block plus two printed strings) — corrected there too, verified label-only since every numeric token in its output is identical before and after.

## [1.2] Circular cross-check — fixed in playground docs

Verified arithmetically rather than accepted: inverting both routes gives 0.0300 vs 0.0298 µm²/bit, ratio 1.0066. Same cell, same ~30% overhead; the 0.7% is 1 MiB-vs-10⁶ rounding. My round-1 claim that the routes "share only the process node" was simply wrong. `crosscheck_area.py` now states this in its docstring and **prints the inversion**, so the circularity is visible rather than buried, and the narrower thing it does establish (my 70% constant matches the industry convention) is stated as exactly that. No delivered number is affected — the answer quotes the cells-only figure, which carries no efficiency assumption.

## One consequence worth flagging

The [1.1] fix pushed the answer to 382 words, over the 380 ceiling. I cut "and no choice of material moves that floor" — the new HP-variant sentence now carries that point concretely, so the clause had become an abstract restatement of what preceded it, the R8 pattern. Now 374 by my method, ~369 by the validator's count (which runs ~5 lower).

Compile rc=0, one page, zero over/underfull boxes; I re-rendered and read the page. Lint passes with `answer.tex` as the only file. `notes.md` and `submission.md` both record the round-2 response.
